all_of: the application issues a session cookie after a successful login
the cookie value decodes to readable structured data rather than an opaque identifier
no signature, MAC or second cookie accompanies the value
any_of: an authenticated page states which privilege the current user lacks
self-registration is open, so a known-plaintext cookie can be obtained

chain.action: fetch the entry page and the login and register pages, list every form action
chain.why: the form actions are the only endpoints; there is no front-end JS calling anything else

chain.action: register an account of your own and log in with it, keeping the Set-Cookie header
chain.why: a cookie whose plaintext you chose is what makes the encoding readable in one step

chain.action: URL-decode then base64-decode the cookie value and look for your own username in it
chain.why: a structured value containing your username proves the session is client-side state, not a server-side id

chain.action: request the authenticated landing page and read the denial text
chain.why: the denial names the field and the value the authorisation check compares against

chain.action: re-encode the same structure with the privileged value and send it as the cookie
chain.why: with no MAC there is nothing to defeat; the server trusts the decoded value as-is

first_confirming_probe.request: register your own account, log in, then URL-decode and base64-decode the session cookie returned by Set-Cookie
first_confirming_probe.expected: the decoded bytes are readable structured data containing the username you just chose
first_confirming_probe.falsifier: the value is opaque, or a signature or MAC segment travels with it and the server rejects an edited value

blast_radius: one self-registered user row on a shared challenge database. The forge itself is a read with a chosen cookie and mutates nothing. Do not spray usernames; register once and reuse that account.

verification.evidence: the flag was read from the body of GET / on the live target, inside an <h1> element, with the forged cookie attached

reuse_when: a cookie named after a framework session but whose value is not the framework's id format
a cookie value ending in = or %3D, or decoding to JSON, a query string or a serialised object
an authorisation check that appears to read a username or role rather than a lookup key
known_traps: the cookie name lies: PHPSESSID here carried base64 JSON, not a PHP session id, so do not skip decoding because the name looks standard
curl writes the cookie URL-encoded; %3D must be decoded to = before base64 decoding or the decode looks like it failed
re-encode with base64 -w0, since a wrapped line breaks the header
